title: Bug: `macsec/test_deployment.py` fails with `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'replace'`
author: arista-nwolfe
body:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

High

### Description of the bug

`macsec/test_deployment.py::test_scale_rekey` fails on systems where the neighbors are `EosHost`s with:
```
30/07/2026 03:16:04 __init__.pytest_runtest_call             L0040 ERROR  | Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/opt/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/_pytest/python.py", line 1707, in runtest
    self.ihook.pytest_pyfunc_call(pyfuncitem=self)
  File "/opt/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/pluggy/_hooks.py", line 512, in __call__
    return self._hookexec(self.name, self._hookimpls.copy(), kwargs, firstresult)
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/opt/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/pluggy/_manager.py", line 120, in _hookexec
    return self._inner_hookexec(hook_name, methods, kwargs, firstresult)
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/opt/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/pluggy/_callers.py", line 167, in _multicall
    raise exception
  File "/opt/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/pluggy/_callers.py", line 121, in _multicall
    res = hook_impl.function(*args)
          ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/opt/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/_pytest/python.py", line 167, in pytest_pyfunc_call
    result = testfunction(**testargs)
             ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/data/tests/macsec/test_deployment.py", line 41, in test_scale_rekey
    _, _, _, dut_egress_sa_table_orig[dut_port], dut_ingress_sa_table_orig[dut_port] = get_appl_db(
                                                                                       ^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/data/tests/common/macsec/macsec_helper.py", line 125, in get_appl_db
    host_sci = get_sci(host.get_dut_iface_mac(host_port_name))
               ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/data/tests/common/macsec/macsec_helper.py", line 70, in get_sci
    system_identifier = macaddress.replace(":", "").replace("-", "")
                        ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'replace'
```

The issue is that the previous testlet `macsec/test_deployment.py::test_config_reload` didn't wait long enough after executing it's `config reload` before moving onto the next test.
Because ports are still down `host.get_dut_iface_mac(host_port_name)` ends up returning `None`.

The reason `macsec/test_deployment.py::test_config_reload` doesn't wait long enough is because it's relying on `check_appl_db` as it's check that the ports are back up:
```
config_reload(duthost)
assert wait_until(300, 6, 12, check_appl_db, duthost, ctrl_links, policy, cipher_suite, send_sci)
```

The problem is `check_appl_db` does nothing if the neighbors are `EosHost`s:
https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/blob/master/tests/common/macsec/macsec_helper.py#L203-L208
```
def check_appl_db(duthost, ctrl_links, policy, cipher_suite, send_sci):
    logger.info("Check appl_db start")
    procs = []
    for port_name, nbr in list(ctrl_links.items()):
        if isinstance(nbr["host"], EosHost):
            continue
```
```
30/07/2026 04:20:41 utilities.wait_until                     L0137 DEBUG  | Wait until check_appl_db is True, timeout is 300 seconds, checking interval is 6, delay is 12 seconds
30/07/2026 04:20:41 utilities.wait_until                     L0141 DEBUG  | Delay for 12 seconds first
30/07/2026 04:20:53 utilities.wait_until                     L0147 DEBUG  | Time elapsed: 0.000000 seconds
30/07/2026 04:20:53 macsec_helper.check_appl_db              L0184 INFO   | Check appl_db start
30/07/2026 04:20:53 macsec_helper.check_appl_db              L0198 INFO   | Check appl_db finished
30/07/2026 04:20:53 utilities.wait_until                     L0162 DEBUG  | check_appl_db is True, exit early with True
```

### Steps to Reproduce

Run `macsec/test_deployment.py` on a cluster that has neighbors running `EosHost`

### Actual Behavior and Expected Behavior

`macsec/test_deployment.py::test_config_reload` should wait until ports are back up before moving to the next test.

linkedPullRequests.body:
### Description of PR
Without this interlock test_config_reload ends up finishing the test before the ports come back up causing issues on subsequent tests

Summary:
Fixes #26706

### Test result
202511 - `macsec/test_deployment.py` passes now

### Approach
#### What is the motivation for this PR?
`macsec/test_deployment.py::test_config_reload` completing early causes `macsec/test_deployment.py::test_scale_rekey` to fail due to ports still being down.

#### How did you do it?
Improve the interlock in `macsec/test_deployment.py::test_config_reload` to make sure the macsec ports are up even on `EosHost` nbrs.

#### How did you verify/test it?
Saw `macsec/test_deployment.py` passing all testlets on 202511.
